question: When measuring the resistance of a resistor using an ohmmeter, what does a reading of zero resistance indicate?
solution:
The correct answer is __The resistor is short-circuited**(Option 2)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Zero resistance__ reading in an ohmmeter indicates that the resistor is short-circuited.
 
• A short circuit occurs when there is a direct connection with negligible resistance between the two terminals.
 
• In such cases, the current flows freely, and the resistance is measured as zero.
 
• This is a fault condition as the resistor is not performing its intended function of limiting current.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Open Circuit:**

 
 
• If the resistor is open-circuited, the ohmmeter will display an infinite resistance or no reading.
 
• This indicates a break in the circuit, and no current can flow.
 
 
 
• **Normal Functioning:**
 
 
• A resistor functioning normally will display a finite resistance value as per its specifications.
 
• This value is generally printed on the resistor body or can be verified with a multimeter.
 
 
 
• **Malfunctioning Ohmmeter:**
 
 
• If the ohmmeter is malfunctioning, it may provide incorrect readings, including zero resistance, regardless of the resistor's condition.
 
• Always ensure the ohmmeter is properly calibrated before use.
